html:
The Duwamish are a Coast Salish people of the area that is now Seattle, around Elliott Bay, the Duwamish River and Lake Washington. Their language is Lushootseed.

They lived in cedar longhouses, fished salmon and gathered shellfish. When American settlers founded Seattle in 1851, they named it after Chief Seattle (Si'ahl), a leader of the Duwamish and Suquamish who welcomed them. In 1855 he signed the Treaty of Point Elliott, giving up the land for reservations, but no Duwamish reservation was ever made, and in 1865 the town of Seattle banned Native people from living within it.

The Duwamish Tribe has sought federal recognition for decades without success. Many Duwamish descendants belong to the Muckleshoot and Suquamish tribes. Their neighbours upriver are the Snoqualmie.
